name: ScyllaDB
tagline: C++ rewrite of Cassandra with shard-per-core design; also speaks the DynamoDB API.
description: ScyllaDB re-implements the Cassandra data model and CQL protocol in C++ on the Seastar framework, pinning one shard to each CPU core so it avoids JVM pauses and lock contention. In practice that means far fewer, larger nodes for the same throughput and tighter p99 latencies, which is why teams such as Discord moved trillions of messages onto it. Tablets-based elastic sharding, Raft-managed schema and topology, and the Alternator DynamoDB-compatible API make it a migration target from both Cassandra and DynamoDB. Since the 2025 releases the single product is source-available rather than AGPL: free up to 10 TB and 50 vCPUs, commercial beyond that.

pricing.notes: Self-hosted use free up to 10 TB total storage / 50 vCPUs for non-customers; ScyllaDB Cloud billed per cluster-hour.

scale.notes: Tablets rebalance data automatically as nodes are added; petabyte-scale clusters are publicly documented.

strengths: Shard-per-core architecture delivers low, stable p99 latency without JVM GC pauses
Drop-in CQL compatibility plus a DynamoDB-compatible API (Alternator)
Tablets give fast, automatic rebalancing when scaling out or in
Typically needs several times fewer nodes than Cassandra for the same load
Workload prioritization lets OLTP and batch jobs share a cluster
weaknesses: No longer open source: production use beyond 10 TB / 50 vCPUs requires a commercial license
Same query-first modelling limits as Cassandra; no joins
Some Cassandra features and edge behaviours differ, so migrations need testing
Smaller community and managed-service choice than Cassandra
useCases: Chat and messaging history at very high volume
notIdealFor: Teams that require an OSI-approved open-source license
